learnings.title: Getting dressed
learnings.focus: The daily wrestle with buttons and socks — full of fine motor practice, and the first place a toddler insists on doing it themselves.

themes.title: Buttons, zips, and getting there myself
themes.detail: Doing up a button, working a zip, pulling on socks — the fiddly motor skill getting dressed asks for every day, moving from needing help to graduated help to none at all.

themes.title: Two things, in order
themes.detail: "Vest on, then socks" — a two-part instruction the child has to hold in mind and act on in the right order, with a "why" thrown in when they ask.

themes.title: Naming what's going on
themes.detail: Colours, textures, the names of what's being pulled on and off — narrated out loud, it floods the child with rich, precise words for something they're already looking at.

themes.title: Choosing, and wanting to do it myself
themes.detail: Picking what to wear is one of a toddler's first real choices, and the "me do it" phase that comes with it is healthy — met best with calm, consistent patience rather than a rush.

themes.title: First this, then that
themes.detail: Getting dressed has a natural order — pants before trousers, socks before shoes — and putting words to it ("first... then...") is early sequencing, for real.

learnings.title: Garden & park play
learnings.focus: The part of the day that happens outdoors — running about, balls, mud and whatever's growing — and the only one that asks for the whole body at once.

themes.title: Running, wheeling, out of breath
themes.detail: Outside is where the big movements live — running, climbing, a scooter or a trike, hopping across the grass, balancing along a low wall. It's also the part of the day a child properly gets out of breath, which under-fives need daily rather than weekly.

themes.title: Balls, and getting them where you want
themes.detail: Kicking, throwing, catching — starting as a two-handed scramble at a big ball, and slowly turning into aim: passing to someone, hitting what they meant to hit, judging how hard.

themes.title: Handfuls of the natural world
themes.detail: Leaves, conkers, bark, stones, a snail on the path — picked up, turned over, smelled, carried home in a pocket. Seeds and bulbs that get planted and then checked on for weeks, and the gentleness that comes with something being alive.

themes.title: Weather, seasons and things that push back
themes.detail: Rain on the face, wind moving the trees, mud that sticks and puddles that splash. The same park looks nothing like itself in October and June — and a swing being pushed or a wagon pulled is a child's first honest encounter with a force.

themes.title: Words for what's out there
themes.detail: Outside hands over words nothing indoors does — knobbly, prickly, soggy, damp — because the child is holding the thing while the word for it arrives, and describing what they can see, hear and smell while they're standing in it.

themes.title: Mud, sticks and repeating patterns
themes.detail: Mark-making without paper — fingers through mud, a stick dragged across gravel. And what gets collected tends to get laid out in a line, stick, leaf, stick, leaf, which is the first repeating pattern a child makes for themselves.

learnings.title: Washing & teeth
learnings.focus: The short, repeated bits of the day — hands, face, teeth, the toilet — where a child slowly takes over looking after their own body.

themes.title: Doing it myself
themes.detail: Brushing teeth, washing hands, managing the toilet — the same few jobs every single day, moving from done-for-them, to done-with-help, to done alone without anyone asking.

themes.title: The toilet, at their own pace
themes.detail: Readiness shows itself — noticing a wet nappy, longer dry stretches, saying they need to go — and it goes best as friendly co-operation rather than a deadline somebody else set.

themes.title: Teeth, morning and night
themes.detail: One of the first things in a child's life that happens twice a day, every day, whether they feel like it or not — as much the shape of a habit as a clean mouth.

themes.title: Knowing why, not just when
themes.detail: Washing sticks once the reason comes with it — that hands carry things you can't see, and that looking after your own body is something you do on purpose.

themes.title: Before eating, after the toilet
themes.detail: Two fixed hinges in the day, and a child who has the words for them has somewhere to hang washing — a moment of its own rather than a random interruption.

learnings.title: Drawing & making
learnings.focus: Paper, pens and a box of junk — the quietest stretch of the day, and the one quietly building the hand that will write.

themes.title: The hand that will hold a pencil
themes.detail: Pinching a crayon between thumb and fingers, snipping with scissors, one hand steadily becoming the one that does the fiddly work — the whole apparatus handwriting needs later, built while the child thinks they're just colouring in.

themes.title: Marks that mean something
themes.detail: The point where a scribble stops being a scribble — "that says mummy", the first letter of a name, a pretend list down the side of the page, an amount recorded in whatever squiggles the child invents for it.

themes.title: Colour, and what things feel like
themes.detail: Paint on fingers, clay, fabric, cornflour and mud — colours getting named while they're being used, and materials sorted by hand into the rough and the smooth, the sticky and the dry.

themes.title: Having an idea, then making it
themes.detail: Rummaging through the box before settling on what it's going to be, a circle that turns into a face, a cereal box that is definitely a rocket — the thing carries an idea the child had first.

themes.title: Shapes that stack and fit
themes.detail: Blocks, inset puzzles, the flat-sided piece that goes on the bottom and the pointy one that makes the roof — shape learned by whether it works, long before it's learned by name.

themes.title: Talk while the hands are busy
themes.detail: One of the calmest talking stretches in the day — hands occupied, heads side by side — and the words that come with it, up and down and round and back, land attached to something actually being done.

learnings.title: Bedtime
learnings.focus: The quietest stretch of the day, and the one that carries more books, rhymes and settling than any other.

themes.title: The story before lights out
themes.detail: A book at the end of the day, the same favourites asked for again and again, joining in with the lines they know by heart — and afterwards, who in it was brave and who was kind.

themes.title: Words that only live in books
themes.detail: Stories carry words the day never says out loud — enormous, invitation, caterpillar — and the back-and-forth about what's happening on the page is where a child picks them up.

themes.title: How a book works
themes.detail: Which way up it goes, the cover and whose name is on it, words running along the line, pages turning in order — all soaked up from being the one holding it.

themes.title: Rhymes and songs at the end of the day
themes.detail: The wind-down songs and the rhymes that always come next — the rhythm of them, the beats inside words, and the last word of a line filled in before it arrives.

themes.title: The same order, every night
themes.detail: Bath, pyjamas, teeth, two stories, lights out — an order a child comes to know well enough to say what's coming next, and the before / then / after that words that ride along with it.

themes.title: Settling down
themes.detail: Winding down with someone calm close by, the blanket or bear that has to be within reach, and sleep quietly taking its place among the things a child knows keep them well.

learnings.title: Chatting & conversation
learnings.focus: Every ordinary chat along the way — in the car, over toys, on the walk to nowhere in particular — and the huge amount of thinking, feeling and connecting that happens inside it.

themes.title: The back-and-forth of a real conversation
themes.detail: It starts as a coo answered with a coo, long before there are any words, and grows into holding an exchange across several turns and changing the subject — even getting the grammar wrong in exactly the way that shows a rule has just been picked up ("I runned really fast").

themes.title: Words for what's going on inside — and what keeps them well
themes.detail: Happy, sad, angry, worried — the words that let a feeling be said instead of only acted out — alongside noticing that someone else might be feeling something different, and picking up the everyday facts of staying well: sleep, food, teeth, moving about, not too much screen.

themes.title: Wondering, guessing and why
themes.detail: A real guess offered to "I wonder what would happen if…", ideas joined together with because and so, more of what's been noticed said aloud with a wider vocabulary than just "thing" or "look", and a problem explained out loud after it's been solved.

themes.title: Who's who in my life
themes.detail: Family, and the wider people who make up their world, named and described — the different shapes a family can take, and their own place in it: a life pieced together from a photo and a story about before they can remember, and starting to feel like someone who matters in all of it.

themes.title: People are different, and that's ordinary
themes.detail: Skin, hair, dress, names, ways of doing things — noticed straightforwardly rather than skipped over, and met with the same interest and warmth as anything else in the world worth talking about.

learnings.title: Following instructions & helping
learnings.focus: The stretch of the day where a request turns into an action — fetching, tidying, waiting a turn — and where a child starts doing it because they understood, not because they were shown.

themes.title: Doing what's asked, first time
themes.detail: "Get your shoes and wait by the door" — holding a two-part instruction in mind and acting on both parts in order, with a "why" answered when they ask. Understanding runs ahead of what a child can say back, so they're following far more than they could yet explain.

themes.title: Finding it from the words alone
themes.detail: "The bag is under the table" — working out where something is from the words alone, no pointing, no showing. A test of listening rather than looking.

themes.title: A real job, not a pretend one
themes.detail: Fetching the milk, washing their own plate after snack, watering something that's growing — a task that actually needs doing, handed over because they can do it, not because it keeps them busy. Checking on a seed or bulb over the weeks it takes to grow adds patience to the job.

themes.title: Remembering the rule without being asked
themes.detail: The agreed rule of the house or the setting, kept without an adult saying it again — the quiet sign that a rule has actually landed, not just been heard.

themes.title: Lining up, queuing, waiting a turn
themes.detail: The everyday choreography of being somewhere with other people — standing in line, waiting to be served, taking a turn and giving one back — managed with a little more patience each time.

learnings.title: Shopping
learnings.focus: The trip that turns number into something real — how many, is it enough, which one's bigger — worked out with actual things in your hands rather than on paper.

themes.title: Working it out on the spot
themes.detail: Real, out-loud number problems that come up in the aisle — is that enough satsumas for the week, how many more we need — worked out with the actual things going into the trolley rather than on paper.

themes.title: Enough for everyone
themes.detail: One for you, one for your sister, is there a spare — sharing out fairly is a real-world problem too, and shopping hands over a fresh one every trip.

themes.title: The numeral and the pile
themes.detail: A number on a list, a price label, a checkout screen — matched to a counted-out pile of the real thing, and read back the other way: however many ends up in the bag is the numeral it stands for.

themes.title: Bigger, smaller, heavier, lighter
themes.detail: The big cabbage against the small one, the heavy bag against the light one — sized up by eye and by hand, with the words that come with it.

learnings.title: Playing with others
learnings.focus: The play that happens shoulder to shoulder with another child — games, pretend, patience, and the occasional falling out that gets talked through.

themes.title: Finding your way into a game
themes.detail: From two-and-a-bit, children start seeking each other out rather than just playing side by side — and a shared pretend idea gets picked up, added to and carried on together rather than staying just one child's.

themes.title: Deciding who's who and making it up as you go
themes.detail: Who's the mummy, who's the dog, what happens next — roles get chosen, argued over and settled, and the story gets narrated out loud as it's acted out, in voices and sentences borrowed for the part.

themes.title: Waiting, joining in, playing by the rules
themes.detail: The wait for a turn without grabbing, joining a group game whether it was someone else's idea or an adult's, and later on, games that come with actual rules and something to aim for.

themes.title: Falling out, and finding a way through it
themes.detail: A disagreement listened to rather than smoothed over, a compromise reached with help, and a growing sense of how the other child might be feeling — all of it building toward relationships that hold up over time.

themes.title: Spotting the pattern without counting
themes.detail: Dice, dominoes, a board game's little grid of dots — glanced at and named instantly, without stopping to count them one by one.

learnings.title: Boundaries & feelings
learnings.focus: The moments feelings run high and a boundary holds anyway — where a child starts naming what's going on inside them, and finds their way back after it's passed.

themes.title: Words for what's going on inside
themes.detail: Cross, worried, happy, sad — the words that let a big feeling be said instead of only shown, and the start of a child noticing it in themselves before somebody else has to point it out.

themes.title: No, and I'll do it myself
themes.detail: The toddler "no" and the insistence on doing it without help — a normal, healthy stretch of finding out where they end and everyone else begins, inside boundaries that stay calm and the same every time.

themes.title: Waiting for a turn
themes.detail: The first taste of holding back rather than grabbing — a minute held onto, "your turn's coming" believed rather than argued with — the earliest form of self-control, built well before it's easy.

themes.title: Coming back down
themes.detail: From needing someone close by to settle, to a few deep breaths remembered alone — calming down starts as something done together and slowly becomes something a child can do for themselves, the size of the reaction gradually catching up to the size of the thing that caused it.

themes.title: Because, so that, I think
themes.detail: The words that carry a reason rather than just a fact — "because...", "so that..." — the beginning of explaining what's happening rather than only reacting to it.

themes.title: Falling out, and finding a way back
themes.detail: A disagreement with another child, listened to and talked through rather than smoothed over — and a mistake taken as an ordinary part of getting better at something, not proof that something's gone wrong.

learnings.title: Bath & water play
learnings.focus: A tub, a couple of cups and something to pour with — the everyday place a child first works out bigger, smaller and which one holds more.

themes.title: Bigger, smaller, heavier
themes.detail: Showing with hands and saying it in words — "bigger", "smaller", "tall", "heavy" — comparing one thing in the water against another, the first informal measuring talk.

themes.title: Which cup holds more
themes.detail: Two containers side by side, and a question that gets answered by pouring rather than counting — the everyday version of capacity, worked out with cups, jugs and whatever's floating in the tub.

themes.title: Longer, heavier, more of it
themes.detail: A sponge, a duck, a toy boat — sized up directly against another rather than against a memory of what came before, weighed in the hand or laid end to end.

themes.title: A guess, then the pour that checks it
themes.detail: Which one turns out to hold more — guessed first, then tested by pouring — and the word that reports the result: this one holds more than that one.

learnings.title: Out & about
learnings.focus: The trips beyond the front door — the walk to the shops, the school run, the bus into town — and the wider world only met by going out into it.

themes.title: Reading the way there
themes.detail: Road signs, shop names, bus numbers and the first letter of their own name — print starting to mean something, spotted on the pavement rather than taught at a table. Alongside it, a route walked often enough to describe back, and the pavement manners that keep the walk safe: holding hands, crossing carefully, staying alert to bikes and scooters.

themes.title: New words for what's out there
themes.detail: Pointing and naming together, then whole sentences about what's just been seen, heard or smelled — and the unusual, precise words only the outside world hands over, like stroll and knobbly.

themes.title: Wondering out loud
themes.detail: A conversation that runs for several turns and changes subject on its own, and the open "I wonder what would happen if..." questions a walk keeps supplying answers to.

themes.title: Weather and living things met along the way
themes.detail: Rain, wind, a change of season noticed trip to trip, and the plants and creatures encountered outside the garden — handled gently, looked at closely, and talked about using words that only apply once you're standing in it.

themes.title: The people and places along the way
themes.detail: Different people noticed and asked about — straightforwardly, building positive attitudes rather than awkwardness — the jobs people do, the family and community talked about on the way, and the odd place that turns out to matter to somebody.
